Poland’s relative tolerance, the growth of towns, and the influence of Renaissance humanism created a space for new natural philosophy. Yet political instability, papal authority, and concern about heresy meant radical ideas still needed careful framing. Copernicus, a canon and intellectual in this complex world, proposed a heliocentric model that was not simply cactiform but mathematical and cautious.
